changed.title: Week of October 26, 2026 (Service release 2610)
changed.text:
App management
Manage referenced apps on AOSP devices
Microsoft Intune now supports AOSP referenced app type that lets you identify an app by package name instead of uploading an APK on AOSP devices. You can assign Required or Uninstall intent to OEM, preloaded, or externally deployed apps that already exist on supported AOSP devices. Required makes an existing app unhidden, while Uninstall hides it. You'll also be able to target referenced apps with JSON-based app configuration policies; Configuration designer and Connected Apps won't be supported. This capability will help organizations manage device-resident apps without adding a new app distribution path.
Applies to:
Android
Device configuration
Enforce Routes capability in Apple VPN profiles
Microsoft Intune now supports Apple's Enforce Routes capability in iOS/iPadOS and macOS VPN profiles. Admins define routing behavior with Include all networks and Exclude local networks, and Intune automatically derives the appropriate Enforce Routes configuration. This helps reduce VPN traffic bypass and de-cloaking risks while keeping routing behavior consistent with Apple's platform semantics.
For more information, see Add VPN settings to Apple devices in Microsoft Intune.
Applies to:
iOS/iPadOS
macOS
Legacy Apple MDM software update workloads removed from Intune
Microsoft Intune is removing legacy Apple MDM software update workloads after Apple retired the underlying commands and payloads in OS 27. Admins should use Apple declarative device management update policies to continue managing software updates. This keeps Intune UI, Graph, and documentation aligned with supported Apple capabilities and provides a clearer path for future update deployments.
For more information, see Move to declarative device management for Apple software updates.
Applies to:
iOS/iPadOS
macOS
Add support for the MEFERI OEMConfig app on Android Enterprise
Microsoft Intune now supports the MEFERI OEMConfig app (com.meferi.oemconfig) for Android Enterprise devices. Admins can use the existing Intune OEMConfig workflow to deploy settings exposed by MEFERI's OEM-provided schema, expanding supported device management options without custom workarounds. Add the app from Managed Google Play, assign it, and create an OEMConfig profile for the bundle.
For more information, see Use OEMConfig on Android Enterprise devices in Microsoft Intune.
Applies to:
Android Enterprise
Device enrollment
Setup Assistant legacy deprecation for Apple enrollment profiles
Intune has ended support for Setup Assistant (legacy) authentication for iOS/iPadOS and macOS automated device enrollment (ADE) with user affinity to align with modern authentication standards. Existing profiles are automatically updated to Setup Assistant with modern authentication, and the legacy option is no longer available when creating or editing profiles; already-enrolled devices remain enrolled and aren't affected.
Applies to:
iOS/iPadOS
macOS
Device management
Administrator protection settings in Account protection policies
Microsoft Intune now includes two Administrator protection settings in endpoint security Account protection policies. On supported Windows 11 versions, admins can configure the Administrator Approval Mode type and choose the elevation prompt behavior for Administrator protection.
For more information, see Account protection policy.
Applies to:
Windows 11
Push notification support update for Windows devices
We've improved connectivity for scenarios that rely on push notifications including Device actions, Win32 apps, PowerShell scripts and Remediations. For the best experience, we recommend updating firewall rules to include this new endpoint:
*.trouter.communications.svc.cloud.microsoft
For the current list of required network endpoints, see Network requirements for PowerShell scripts and Win32 apps and Windows Push Notification Services (WNS) dependencies in the Intune endpoints documentation.
Applies to:
Windows
Apple OS 27 DDM status data added to device inventory
Microsoft Intune now adds Apple OS 27 declarative device management status data to device inventory. Admins can review new inventory for: device health for hardware components, enhanced logging sessions, content cache status, and Apple MDM and security states such as enrollment type, awaiting configuration, and lockdown mode. Values depend on supported OS, hardware, enrollment, and DDM capabilities.
Applies to:
Apple devices running OS 27
Device security
STIG audit baselines for Windows devices in commercial tenants
Microsoft Intune commercial tenants can now audit Windows devices against Security Technical Implementation Guide (STIG) recommendations. Review per-setting and per-device audit results to identify configuration gaps and prioritize remediation. The baseline evaluates supported automated checks without changing device settings.
This feature requires Intune Advanced Analytics. Assess rules that require manual verification separately.
For more information, see Use STIG audit baselines to assess Windows device compliance.
Applies to:
Windows
Updated Windows support for Administrator protection settings
Microsoft Intune now supports two Administrator protection settings in the settings catalog on Windows 11 versions 24H2 and 25H2. Admins can configure the Administrator Approval Mode type and choose the elevation prompt behavior used with Administrator protection.
For more information, see Settings catalog.
Applies to:
Windows 11
Agent runtime protection settings are generally available
Microsoft Intune's endpoint security template for Microsoft Defender for Endpoint agent runtime protection settings is now generally available. Administrators can use the template to manage supported runtime protection settings for Windows devices without the preview designation, aligning Intune policy management with the Microsoft Defender for Endpoint general availability release. We have also added a new setting called AI agent runtime inspection to be configured in the template.
Applies to:
Windows
Monitor and troubleshoot
Certificate connector health monitoring in the Microsoft Intune admin center
The Certificate Connector for Microsoft Intune now surfaces health and status signals in the Microsoft Intune admin center, so you can spot certificate-issuance problems early. Clear indicators call out common failure conditions — such as the connector being unable to reach the certification authority (CA), the connector's service account lacking permission to issue or revoke certificates, or certificate requests being rejected because of a template mismatch with your PKCS profile. Each signal includes guidance to help you investigate and remediate before devices relying on certificate-based authentication hit access, sign-in, or compliance issues.
For more information, see Certificate Connector for Microsoft Intune.
Applies to:
Certificate Connector for Microsoft Intune
Scripts
Faster delivery of Windows scripts
Microsoft Intune now uses push notifications for admin-initiated and service-side changes to Windows scripts. Managed devices can check in sooner after script changes, reducing delivery and refresh delays compared with waiting for the normal polling interval. This update improves script deployment responsiveness without requiring a new admin workflow.
Applies to:
Windows

new.title: Preserve managed apps with Return to Service
new.text: Devices erased with Return to Service can now keep their managed apps through the erase, so a redeployed device is ready for its next user without re-downloading every app. Admins turn on the new Allow app preservation during Return to Service option in the Automated Device Enrollment Library Item for iPhone and iPad. Devices running iOS or iPadOS 26 or later then show a Preserve managed apps option, checked by default, in the Erase device modal after Use Return to Service is selected. Only managed-app executables are kept; all user data, including each app's own stored data, is still erased. The option is also available through the Iru Enterprise API's erase action, and as an admin-controlled default for end-user-triggered Return to Service through Self Service.

new.title: Delegate certificate management to Google Play apps on Android
new.text: Admins can now give a Google Play app permission to manage certificates on managed Android devices. A new Certificate management section on the Google Play app Library Item lets you allow an app to install and manage certificates, to select certificates for other apps, or both. This supports running a third-party certificate or PKI app on managed Android devices. Only one app per device can select certificates for other apps, so the Blueprint editor blocks assigning two such apps to the same Blueprint node and warns when two apps on the same path could reach the same device.

new.text:
Configure Extensible Single Sign-On Profile
The DDM SSO payload enables administrators to configure and deploy Single Sign-On (SSO) settings through Apple's Declarative Device Management (DDM) framework. It allows administrators to define the required SSO app extensions and their associated configurations, which are delivered to enrolled devices as declarative settings. This enables devices to receive and manage SSO configurations through DDM rather than relying solely on the traditional profile-based deployment mechanism.
note
Supported OS Version: iOS 27.0 and iPadOS 27.0 or later
Supported Enrollment Types:
Device Enrollment and Automated Device Enrollment
User Enrollment
To configure an app extension that performs Single Sign-On on enrolled devices, follow these steps:
On the SureMDM Web Console, navigate to Profile > iOS/iPadOS > Add > Select Enrollment Type > Identity and Access Management > Extensible Single Sign-On > Configure.
Enter a Profile Name and click Add.
Configure Single Sign-On Settings and click Add.
SettingsDescription
SSO Provider
Choose the identity provider responsible for handling Single Sign-On authentication for this configuration.
Microsoft Enterprise SSO via Company Portal App - When selected, SureMDM automatically populates the required values for the Company Portal.
Manual Configuration - When selected, the administrator must manually configure the required settings.
Extension Identifier
Enter the bundle Id of the app extension that performs single sign-on for the specified URLs.
Applicable only if Manual Configuration is selected as SSO Provider.
Single Sign-On Type
Select the SSO type.
- Credential
- Redirect
Applicable only if Manual Configuration is selected as SSO Provider.
Realm
Enter the Realm name for the credential payload.
Applicable only if Manual Configuration is selected as SSO Provider and Credential as Single Sign-On Type.
Host
Enter the array of hostnames or domain names that are authenticated using app extensions.
Applicable only if Manual Configuration is selected as SSO Provider and Credential as Single Sign-On Type.
URLs
An array of URL prefixes of identity providers where the app extension performs SSO.
Shared Device Mode
Enable this option to configure Microsoft Authenticator in Shared Device mode for a seamless user experience and secure sharing across the organization. Available in iOS 14.0 / iPadOS 14.0 or later.
Applicable only if Microsoft Authenticator for SSO is selected as SSO Provider.
ExtensionData
Enter a dictionary of arbitrary data to be passed to the app extension as key-value pairs.
Click Save.
The newly created profile will be listed in the Profiles section.
Go back to the Home tab and select the iOS/iPadOS device(s) or group(s).
Click Apply to launch the Apply Job/Profile To Device prompt.
In the Apply Job/Profile To Device prompt, select the created profile and click Apply.

changed.title: profile owner
changed.text:
Profile Owner
With the adoption of Profile Owner (Personally Owned Devices), businesses are offering their employees freedom to use their mobile devices for both personal as well as official use. Personally Owned Devices enables personal devices to have ready access to business data anytime, from anywhere.
SureMDM integration with Android Enterprise provides a flexible and effective solution to enable employee personal phones for work and counter security risks that come with it.
There are two ways to enroll devices in SureMDM using Work Profile:
Using Gmail Account
Using Managed Google Account
In order to proceed, ensure that your SureMDM account is enrolled with Android Enterprise. Refer to the Enroll SureMDM with Android Enterprise section for detailed instructions.
note
For devices enrolled in Profile Owner mode, all configurations applied from SureMDM are enforced on the managed device profile. These configurations will not affect the device's personal profile or personal data.

Using Gmail Account (PO)
In order to proceed, ensure that your SureMDM account is enrolled with Android Enterprise. Refer to the Enroll SureMDM with Android Enterprise section for detailed instructions.
Once the SureMDM account is enrolled with Android Enterprise, the device also needs to get enrolled with the Android Enterprise account. This process gets started with configuring the SureMDM Agent with Android Enterprise.
To enroll Android devices in SureMDM using Android Work Profile Enrollment, follow the below-mentioned steps:
note
Work Profile Enrollment will be supported only on Android 6 and above devices.
Download SureMDM Agent app on the device from the following sources:
Google Play
42Gears Website
Open the SureMDM Agent app and tap Get Started.
Tap Work Profile Enrollment.
Select one of the following options on the next screen:
A. SureMDM Account ID - Use this option to register the device manually.
Enter the SureMDM Account ID and tap Next.
note
Account ID is the unique identification number of the SureMDM account. It can be copied from the SureMDM Console, i.e., Navigate to Settings on the top right corner in SureMDM console to get Account ID.
Server Path is the SureMDM console URL to which the devices will be enrolled.
Enter the Server Path and tap Next.
Select one of the following options to set the device name on the Configure Device Name screen and tap Register.
Set Device Name Manually
Use MAC Address
Use System Generated Name
Tap Accept \& continue to create a work profile on the device.
Once done, tap Next to complete the enrollment process.
B. Scan QR - Use this option if you are already logged into the SureMDM Web Console and want to enroll the device into SureMDM.
Navigate to the Enrollment menu > QR Code Enrollment on the SureMDM Web Console.
Create a QR code for QR code for Work Profile Enrollment.
Scan the QR code on the device to enroll.
When the device is enrolled , admins will notice the following:
On the device side, a Work Container will be created, and the SureMDM Agent will be visible in the workspace with briefcase icon.
On the SureMDM console, under the Device Info panel > Android Enterprise, the Profile Owner tag will be shown.

The integration of SureMDM with Android Enterprise offers a versatile and efficient solution, enabling personal use on company-owned devices while maintaining effective management.

changed.text:
Near Field Communication (NFC) enrollment enables administrators to quickly provision and enroll Android devices by simply tapping an NFC tag on a factory reset device. This method simplifies large-scale device deployment by automatically configuring Wi-Fi settings, downloading the required management application, verifying the application package, and enrolling the device into the SureMDM console without manual configuration. Using NFC-based provisioning helps reduce setup time, minimize configuration errors, and streamline the enrollment process for enterprise deployments. The NFC tag contains all the required provisioning details, allowing devices to be configured automatically during the initial setup process. Write Data to NFC Tag NFC provisioning simplifies Android device enrollment by allowing administrators to configure devices using a pre-written NFC tag. Follow the steps below to write provisioning data to an NFC tag: Open any NFC configuration application to write the NFC tag. Navigate to the Write tab. Tap on Add a Record and select Data. In the Text field, enter: application In the Plain field, enter: com.android.managedprovisioning In the Data field, enter the provisioning data using the format given below: android.app.extra.PROVISIONING_DEVICE_ADMIN_PACKAGE_DOWNLOAD_LOCATION=[Add NFC Tool Link Here]
android.app.extra.PROVISIONING_DEVICE_ADMIN_SIGNATURE_CHECKSUM=[Add Checksum Here]
android.app.extra.PROVISIONING_DEVICE_ADMIN_COMPONENT_NAME=com.nix/com.nix.NixDeviceAdmin
android.app.extra.PROVISIONING_WIFI_SSID="[Enter Wi-Fi SSID]"
android.app.extra.PROVISIONING_WIFI_SECURITY_TYPE=[Enter Security Type]
android.app.extra.PROVISIONING_WIFI_PASSWORD=[Enter Wi-Fi Password]
android.app.extra.PROVISIONING_ADMIN_EXTRAS_BUNDLE=nfc_data:
AccountId:[Enter Account ID]; ServerPath:[Enter Server Path];
HttpHeader:https://; EnrollmentType:1;
EnrollmentMode:0;GroupPath:[Enter Group Path]

 Click OK to save the record. note Ensure all data fields are accurate and accessible to avoid provisioning failure. Follow the steps below to provision a device using an NFC tag: Ensure the device is in factory reset mode. Tap the NFC tag at the appropriate location on the target device. Enroll SureMDM with Android Enterprise
To use the full potential of Android Enterprise's robust device management features, it is necessary to enroll your SureMDM account with Android Enterprise. By doing so, you gain access to a wide array of capabilities to efficiently manage and control your Android devices. There are two methods through which SureMDM can be enrolled with Android Enterprise:
Using Gmail Account
Using Managed Google Account
Using Gmail Account
To enroll SureMDM account with Android Enterprise, follow these steps:
On the SureMDM Web Console, navigate to Settings > Account Settings > Android Management > Android Enterprise Enrollment.
On Android Enterprise Enrollment page, click Enroll Android Enterprise.
Select Google Play EMM API.
Select Enroll Using Your Gmail Account and click Enroll.
On the Google Play page, click Get Started to login with the Gmail account.
Enter organization's name in the Business Name field and click Next.
Enter EU Representative details: Name, Email, Phone, select Terms and Conditions checkbox, and click Confirm.
A message will be displayed on completion of the Android Enterprise setup.
Click Complete Registration.
Once Android Enterprise enrolled to the SureMDM account, the following options are available in Account Settings > Android Management > Android Enterprise Enrollment:
Managed Google Play Account Information: Displays details about the linked managed Google Play account
Store Layout - Admin can use the basic layout or create a new page to display all Enterprise Approved Apps.
Application Licenses - This option provides summary of your application licenses.
Zero-touch iframe - This option allows you to set up your devices using zero-touch accounts.
Unenroll - Allows to Unenroll your existing Google Managed Domain.
Using Managed Google Account
To enroll the SureMDM account with Android Enterprise, follow these steps:
On the SureMDM Web Console, navigate to Settings > Account Settings > Android Management > Android Enterprise Enrollment.
On Android Enterprise Enrollment page, click Enroll Android Enterprise.

changed.text:
Linux Enrollment
The first step in managing your Linux devices is to enroll them in SureMDM. Once registered, you can effortlessly apply policies and manage devices remotely.
Supported Linux Distributions
Arch Linux
CentOS (version 10)
Debian
Fedora (versions 38, 39, 40, 41)
Linux Mint (versions 18, 19, 20, 21, 22)
Linux Mint Debian Edition (LMDE)
Omarchy
Oracle Linux (versions 8, 9)
Raspberry Pi OS
Red Hat Enterprise Linux (versions 8, 9, 10)
Rocky Linux (versions 8, 9, 10)
SUSE
Ubuntu (versions 16, 18, 19, 20, 22, 24, 26.04)
Prerequisites
OpenJDK: Version 7 OR above. Click here for more information.
Oracle JDK: Version 7 OR above. Click here for more information.
Important
Before installing the SureMDM Agent on Ubuntu-based devices, ensure that the lxd group is not present. Membership in the lxd group allows non-privileged users to access LXD container features, which can be used to perform root-level operations. This poses a security risk, including potential exploitation of the SureMDM Agent. To mitigate this risk, remove the group using the command: sudo groupdel lxd and then proceed with the enrollment.
Linux CLI Based Enrollment
Linux CLI (Command Line Interface) Based Enrollment is a method employed to onboard devices, systems, or users into a network or service within a Linux environment, using command-line commands and tools. This approach grants administrators precise control and automation for device and user management in Linux environments, allowing them to script and execute commands efficiently and consistently. It streamlines the registration process, enhancing system security and network integrity.
To register Linux devices using the command-line interface (CLI), follow these steps
On the SureMDM Web Console, navigate to Enrollment > Manual Enrollment > Linux.
Click Configure to customize/set up the Enrollment operations. The Enrollment Configuration displays.
Enter the required details to configure as per the requirement:
Enrollment ConfigurationDescription
Enrollment Group Path
Indicates the specific group within the SureMDM console where the device will be registered.
Device Name Type
1. System Generated Name: Utilizes the system-generated name.
2. Host Name: Utilizes the device's hostname.
3. Serial Number: Generates a unique serial number for the device.
4. Manual Name: Requires users to provide a custom name during enrollment, which will be displayed on the console.
Note: Selecting Manual Name prompts the user to enter the device name on the Terminal screen during enrollment. The completion of enrollment is only possible after entering this value.
Advanced Settings
1. Proxy Configuration: Allows entry of the proxy address.
2. Use UUID as Device Identifier: Enables the use of UUID as the device identifier when registering with SureMDM.
Once you have configured the settings, click Apply.
Once the configurations have been set in the Enrollment Configuration popup, the CLI command will appear in the text area in encoded format. Simply choose the "Copy Command" option to proceed.
Now, open the Terminal application in the target device:
You can directly open the Terminal by pressing Ctrl + Alt + T
or
Alternatively, locate it among your installed programs by clicking on the "Show Applications" option in the bottom left corner of your screen. Type "Terminal" and press Enter to find and launch the Terminal shortcut.
Next, paste the previously copied command into the Terminal window and press Enter. This will begin the enrollment process for your Linux device, ensuring successful registration.
note
'CLI Based Enrollment' is supported from SureMDM Agent Version 3.8.0 onwards.
On the SureMDM web console, the device will start reflecting under the Device Grid.
You will know the device has been enrolled in SureMDM when:
On the SureMDM Agent Home Screen, the device status changes to Online.
On the SureMDM Web Console, the device appears under the Device Grid.

changed.text:
Bixolon Printer Enrollment
42Gears has enabled seamless integration of Bixolon printers with the SureMDM console to simplify device management and improve operational efficiency. Through this integration, administrators can remotely enroll, configure, and monitor Bixolon printers from a single centralized platform. It provides enhanced visibility and control, helping reduce manual effort and maintain consistent printer performance across deployments. By managing Bixolon printers via SureMDM, organizations can streamline operations, reduce maintenance overhead, and ensure smooth and reliable printing processes.
Enroll Bixolon Printer to SureMDM
To enroll the Bixolon Printers in SureMDM Console, follow these steps:
Prerequisites
Enable Things Gateway in the SureMDM Console.
The host machine and Bixolon printer should be connected to the same network.
Steps:
Obtain the Printer’s IP address from the Bixolon printer display.
Run this IP address in the browser to open the Bixolon tool and Log in using the credentials
note
The default username “admin” and the password should be set by the user.
Click on the Configure tab in the Menu bar and Navigate to the Protocol Configuration Settings and enable MQTT.
Navigate to the MQTT Configuration settings to set up the MQTT by entering the following details:
a. MQTT Broker Address - It is the host address or URL of the MQTT broker to connect to.
The values vary based on the region as follows:
If your SureMDM URL is dns.suremdm.io (US), then use the server mqttbrokerusdns.suremdm.io
If your SureMDM URL is dns.eu.suremdm.io (EU), then use the server mqttbrokereu.eu.suremdm.io
If your SureMDM URL is dns.in.suremdm.io (IN), then use the server mqttbrokerin.in.suremdm.io
If your SureMDM URL is dns.eu2.suremdm.io (EU2), then use the server mqttbrokereu.eu2.suremdm.io
If your SureMDM URL is dns.me.suremdm.io (ME), then use the server mqttbrokerme.me.suremdm.io
If your SureMDM URL is suremdm.42gears.com (US Master), then use the server mqttbrokerusmaster.42gears.com
b. MQTT Port - It is the network port used to establish communication between the device and the MQTT broker.
The values are the same for all the regions, i.e., 8883
c. MQTT Authentication - It is the process of verifying the identity of a client before allowing it to connect to an MQTT broker.
Select Enable from the dropdown.
d. CA Certificate - It is a digital certificate used to verify whether a server or client certificate can be trusted.
Enable the CA certificate checkbox and upload the certificate by choosing the file from the system.
note
Navigate to Enrollment > Manual Enrollment > Things > Bixolon Printer in the SureMDM console to download the CA Certificate.

note

f. MQTT User Password - Password for MQTT broker authentication. Value here is the MQTT Gateway password.
note
The Gateway Password can be copied from the Enable Things Gateway section.
g. MQTT Tenant ID - Identifier used to associate the device with a specific tenant/environment. Value here is the SureMDM account ID.
note
Navigate to Settings on the top right corner of the SureMDM console to get the Account ID.
h. MQTT QoS - Defines the message delivery guarantee level.
note
Enter value as 2.
note
Checkbox should be enabled for MQTT User name, MQTT Password and MQTT Tenant ID to enter the values.
Click on the Configure button.
If valid values are entered, the Bixolon printers should get successfully enrolled to the SureMDM Console.

Version Information:
Scalefusion Dashboard: v68.5.0

Release Notes:
Windows Self-Service for App Catalog Apps
Scalefusion now extends Self-Service capabilities to Windows App Catalog applications, allowing IT Administrators to make applications available for end users to install, update, and uninstall.
Administrators can silently install applications while also making them available in the Self-Service catalog. This allows users to reinstall an application if a silent installation encounters an error or install an available update immediately instead of waiting for the automatic update process.
When an application is added to Self-Service, users can also update it whenever the agent detects that a newer version is available.
Additionally, users can now uninstall Enterprise Store applications that are made available through Self-Service.
Linux SUSE Support
Scalefusion now supports the enrollment and management of SUSE-based Linux devices, extending Linux device management support to additional Linux distributions.
Linux Device Management Enhancements
Several enhancements have been introduced to simplify Linux device administration and provide IT Administrators with additional management capabilities:
a. Global Admin Account Creation: IT Administrators can now create a global admin account for Linux devices from the Utilities section, similar to the existing functionality for Windows and macOS.
b. Shutdown Configuration Settings: Administrators can configure a grace period and a warning message displayed to users when a device is shut down remotely through Device Details or Developer APIs.
c. User Account Group Management: IT Administrators can now switch Linux user accounts between Standard and Admin groups from the User Access Management (UAM) section.
d. Bulk Device Renaming: Bulk renaming from the Devices page now supports Linux devices. Administrators can rename Linux devices using either a Rule or a CSV file.
e. Enhanced Location Capturing Options: Linux location tracking now includes IP-based location as an explicit option, and Browser-based location capturing is available again. IP-based location uses a known database to map locations but may not provide accurate results. Browser-based location capturing can consume significant CPU and memory resources and is not recommended unless location accuracy is a critical requirement.
Bug Fixes:
Veltar Secure Web Gateway Compatibility: Resolved interoperability issues between Veltar Secure Web Gateway (SWG) and Cisco VPN, as well as applications that use localhost traffic.

New: Agent Delegated Access
Feature: Agent Delegated Access is now in Private Preview!
We’re extending Agent Identities so an AI agent can authenticate with its own JumpCloud-managed identity while acting on behalf of an end user.
The initial release supports customers building their own agent applications and internal APIs. JumpCloud provides identity and token exchange, and the customer’s API can identify both the user requesting the work and the agent performing it.
Key Highlights & Features:
User delegation: Exchange a trusted user identity token for a signed token representing the agent acting on that user’s behalf.
Admin controls: Enable delegation and select a trusted OIDC application from the agent’s new Delegated access tab.
Allowed audiences: Configure the resources an agent may request tokens for.
Direct API access: Use JumpCloud-issued tokens with customer-controlled APIs without routing those API calls through the AI Gateway.
See Get Started: Agent Delegated Access to learn more.
Enhancement: Capability-based app setup for SSO, SCIM, and MCP
Feature: SSO Applications/AI Gateway
When you add an application, select the capabilities you need: SSO, SCIM, and/or MCP. New apps only show configuration for what you selected.
You can create MCP-only applications that may not use JumpCloud SSO, assign them to user groups for access control, and make the MCP server available through AI Gateway.
For MCP-only access, select Manage MCP Servers. You do not need to configure SSO or create a bookmark.
Use the Actions menu to add SCIM or MCP capabilities if you need them later.
You can also create the application from AI Gateway when you register an MCP server. It follows the same add-application flow.
You can also review a user group’s applications from Identity Management > User Groups. Open the group and select the Applications tab. Apps with validated MCP configs are marked as ready for AI Gateway. Group membership still controls access.
See Get Started: AI Gateway, Get Started: SSO Applications, and Authorize Users to an SSO Application to learn more.

Feature: Access Certification
We are excited to introduce JumpCloud Access Certification, our powerful Identity Governance and Administration (IGA) solution built to make periodic access reviews completely effortless, audit-ready, and secure.
Key Highlights & Features:
Flexible Review Campaigns: Launch one-time or recurring review campaigns tailored for Single Sign-On (SSO) applications or directory user groups with just a few clicks.
Multi-Stage Review Workflows: Establish multi-step approval chains involving Administrators, Managers, Resource Owners, or designated User Groups to ensure thorough access validation.
Automated Remediation: Eliminate manual follow-ups! Set automated policies to immediately revoke access or suspend inactive identities the moment a decision is finalized or when review deadlines expire.
Centralized Admin Queue: Keep admins focused with a consolidated dashboard tracking all pending review and remediation tasks in real time.
Audit-Ready Reporting & Sign-off: Export frozen, tamper-proof campaign snapshots in CSV, JSON, or PDF formats—complete with formal administrator sign-off flows and SHA-256 document hashing for effortless compliance audits.
See Manage Access Certification and Users: Access Certification Campaigns to learn more.

Feature: Policy Management
Manage specific Windows registry values for an assigned user’s profile when JumpCloud doesn’t offer an equivalent built-in policy. Assign it to users or user groups; the Agent applies settings under HKEY_CURRENT_USER when that user signs in. No MDM enrollment or device restart required.
See Create a User Level Windows Custom Registry Keys Policy to learn more.

See Create a User Level Custom Windows MDM (OMA URI) Policy to learn more.

We’ve enhanced the Device Lock MDM command for macOS, iOS, and iPadOS, letting you secure Apple devices with automatic PIN generation and escrow, improved lock status visibility, and support for Lock Screen content.
Automatic PIN escrow (macOS): JumpCloud generates and stores the lock PIN when you lock a Mac, and you can retrieve it later from the Admin Portal under Highlights > Device Lock > View PIN.
Lock Screen contact details: Optionally show a message and phone number on the Lock Screen for Mac computers, iPhone, and iPad.
macOS Lock Status: Track whether a Mac is locked or unlocked from the Devices list using the macOS Lock Status column.
iOS and iPadOS unlock: Per Apple MDM framework, iOS and iPadOS devices unlock with the existing device passcode. JumpCloud does not generate or store a PIN for them.
